'''''Caucalis platycarpos''''' is a species of [[flowering plant]] in the family [[Apiaceae]], the only member of the genus '''''Caucalis'''''. Common names are '''carrot bur parsley''',<ref>{{PLANTS|id=CAPL11|taxon=Caucalis platycarpos|accessdate=11 January 2016}}</ref> '''small bur-parsley''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=2014-10-17 }}</ref> and '''burr parsley.'''<ref>{{cite journal | pmid = 23881052 | doi=10.3390/molecules18078666 | volume=18 | issue=7 | title=Phenolic content and antioxidant activities of burr parsley (Caucalis platycarpos L.) | journal=Molecules | pages=8666–81 | last1 = Plazonić | first1 = A | last2 = Mornar | first2 = A | last3 = Maleš | first3 = Ž | last4 = Kujundžić | first4 = N| year=2013 | pmc = 6269816 | doi-access=free }}</ref> It is native to Europe, North Africa, and the Middle East as far east as Iran.<ref name=yvonne>[http://www.tela-botanica.org/bdtfx-nn-14897-synthese Tela Botanica, Caucalis à feuilles de carotte, ''Caucalis platycarpos'' L.] in French with photo and French distribution map</ref><ref>[http://luirig.altervista.org/flora/taxa/index1.php?scientific-name=caucalis+platycarpos Altervista Flora Italiana, Lappola carota, Kletten-Haftdolde, piggkörvel, ''Caucalis platycarpos'' L.]</ref>

==Description==

''Caucalis platycarpos'' is an [[Annual plant|annual]] up to {{convert|40|cm}} tall with trailing stems. Leaves are highly divided into many small [[leaflet (botany)|leaflets]]. Flowers are produced in an [[umbel]] of 2 to 5 flowers, each with white or pink [[petal]]s. The fruit is an oblong [[Capsule (botany)|capsule]] with many hooked [[Thorns, spines, and prickles|spines]] on the surface.<ref name=yvonne/><ref>[http://www.unavarra.es/herbario/htm/Cauc_plat.htm Herbario de la Universidad Pública de Navarra, Flora Arvense de Navarra, familia Umbelliferae, ''Caucalis platycarpos'' L.] in Spanish, with photos</ref>

== Distribution and habitat==
It is distributed in southwest Asia, North Africa and most of central and Southern Europe; almost all of the Iberian Peninsula.

It is found in crop fields, fallows and nitrophilous grasslands. Preferably in basic substrates at an altitude of 100-1000 (1600) meters. Flowering occurs in March-June (July) and fruiting in May-August.
